name: VG-10
description: VG-10 (V Gold 10) is one of the most popular Japanese stainless steels, developed by Takefu Special Steel. It offers an excellent balance of edge retention, corrosion resistance, and ease of sharpening. Widely used by brands like Shun, Tojiro, and many Sakai makers.

name: AUS-10
description: AUS-10 is a high-carbon stainless steel produced by Aichi Steel. It is similar to VG-10 but slightly easier to sharpen with marginally less edge retention. Popular in mid-range Japanese knives, especially from Seki-based manufacturers.

name: SG2/R2
description: SG2 (Super Gold 2), also marketed as R2, is a powdered metallurgy stainless steel by Takefu Special Steel. With a hardness of 63-64 HRC, it holds an incredibly keen edge while still resisting corrosion. Used in premium knives from Takamura, Saji, and the Shun Premier line.

name: Aogami Super
description: Aogami Super (Blue Super Steel) is the pinnacle of Hitachi's carbon steel line. With tungsten, chromium, and molybdenum additions, it achieves extreme hardness and edge retention. Requires careful maintenance to prevent rust. Favored by professional chefs in Japan who demand the ultimate edge.

name: Aogami #2
description: Aogami #2 (Blue Paper #2) is a popular high-carbon steel by Hitachi Metals. It contains tungsten and chromium for improved edge retention compared to white steel. Easier to sharpen than Aogami Super while still achieving excellent sharpness. A favorite for traditional Japanese knives.

name: Shirogami #2
description: Shirogami #2 (White Paper #2) is the purest form of high-carbon steel from Hitachi Metals. With no additional alloys, it sharpens to an incredibly keen edge with minimal effort. It is the gold standard for traditional single-bevel knives in Sakai. Requires diligent rust prevention.

name: Shirogami #1
description: Shirogami #1 (White Paper #1) has higher carbon content than White #2, resulting in a harder edge with better retention. Slightly more difficult to sharpen but rewards the user with a longer-lasting edge. Preferred by experienced sharpeners and sushi chefs.

name: Ginsan (Silver-3)
description: Ginsan (Silver-3) bridges the gap between carbon and stainless steels. Produced by Hitachi Metals, it offers sharpening characteristics similar to carbon steel while providing stainless-level corrosion resistance. Increasingly popular for high-end single-bevel knives.

name: ZDP-189
description: ZDP-189 is an ultra-high carbon powdered steel by Hitachi Metals, achieving the highest hardness among commonly used knife steels. At 64-67 HRC, it holds an edge for an extraordinarily long time. However, it is notoriously difficult to sharpen and can be brittle. Used in premium knives by makers like Hattori.

name: HAP40
description: HAP40 is a high-speed powdered tool steel originally developed for industrial cutting tools. It offers exceptional edge retention and wear resistance. Due to its semi-stainless nature, it has moderate corrosion resistance. Used by Shun in their premium Dual Core line.
